### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

If you really need to see something from the full command's output, you can redirect output to a file and then search in that file. # hyperfine A command-line benchmarking tool. **Demo**: Benchmarking [`fd`](https://github.com/sharkdp/fd) and [`find`](https://www.gnu.org/software/findutils/): ![hyperfine](https://i.imgur.com/z19OYxE.gif) ### Sponsors A special *thank you* goes to our biggest sponsor:

Warp, the intelligent terminal
Available on MacOS, Linux, Windows ## Features * Statistical analysis across multiple runs. * Support for arbitrary shell commands. * Constant feedback about the benchmark progress and current estimates. * Warmup runs can be executed before the actual benchmark. * Cache-clearing commands can be set up before each timing run. * Statistical outlier detection to detect interference from other programs and caching effects. * Export results to various formats: CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc. * Parameterized benchmarks (e.g. vary the number of threads). * Cross-platform ## Usage ### Basic benchmarks To run a benchmark, you can simply call `hyperfine ...`. The argument(s) can be any shell command. For example: ```sh hyperfine 'sleep 0.3' ``` Hyperfine will automatically determine the number of runs to perform for each command. By default, it will perform *at least* 10 benchmarking runs and measure for at least 3 seconds. To change this, you can use the `-r`/`--runs` option: ```sh hyperfine --runs 5 'sleep 0.3' ``` If you want to compare the runtimes of different programs, you can pass multiple commands: ```sh hyperfine 'hexdump file' 'xxd file' ``` ### Warmup runs and preparation commands For programs that perform a lot of disk I/O, the benchmarking results can be heavily influenced by disk caches and whether they are cold or warm. If you want to run the benchmark on a warm cache, you can use the `-w`/`--warmup` option to perform a certain number of program executions before the actual benchmark: ```sh hyperfine --warmup 3 'grep -R TODO *' ``` Conversely, if you want to run the benchmark for a cold cache, you can use the `-p`/`--prepare` option to run a special command before *each* timing run. For example, to clear harddisk caches on Linux, you can run ```sh sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches ``` To use this specific command with hyperfine, call `sudo -v` to temporarily gain sudo permissions and then call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' 'grep -R TODO *' ``` ### Parameterized benchmarks If you want to run a series of benchmarks where a single parameter is varied (say, the number of threads), you can use the `-P`/`--parameter-scan` option and call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'make clean' --parameter-scan num_threads 1 12 'make -j {num_threads}' ``` This also works with decimal numbers. The `-D`/`--parameter-step-size` option can be used to control the step size: ```sh hyperfine --parameter-scan delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}' ``` This runs `sleep 0.3`, `sleep 0.5` and `sleep 0.7`. For non-numeric parameters, you can also supply a list of values with the `-L`/`--parameter-list` option: ``` hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp' ``` ### Intermediate shell By default, commands are executed using a predefined shell (`/bin/sh` on Unix, `cmd.exe` on Windows). If you want to use a different shell, you can use the `-S, --shell ` option: ```sh hyperfine --shell zsh 'for i in {1..10000}; do echo test; done' ``` Note that hyperfine always *corrects for the shell spawning time*. To do this, it performs a calibration procedure where it runs the shell with an empty command (multiple times), to measure the startup time of the shell. It will then subtract this time from the total to show the actual time used by the command in question. If you want to run a benchmark *without an intermediate shell*, you can use the `-N` or `--shell=none` option. This is helpful for very fast commands (< 5 ms) where the shell startup overhead correction would produce a significant amount of noise. Note that you cannot use shell syntax like `*` or `~` in this case. ``` hyperfine -N 'grep TODO /home/user' ``` ### Shell functions and aliases If you are using bash, you can export shell functions to directly benchmark them with hyperfine: ```bash my_function() { sleep 1; } export -f my_function hyperfine --shell=bash my_function ``` Otherwise, inline them into or source them from the benchmarked program: ```sh hyperfine 'my_function() { sleep 1; }; my_function' echo 'alias my_alias="sleep 1"' > /tmp/my_alias.sh hyperfine '. /tmp/my_alias.sh; my_alias' ``` ### Exporting results Hyperfine has multiple options for exporting benchmark results to CSV, JSON, Markdown and other formats (see `--help` text for details). #### Markdown You can use the `--export-markdown ` option to create tables like the following: | Command | Mean [s] | Min [ 4582 characters elided ecified once for all commands or multiple times, once for each command. .TH HYPERFINE 1
.SH NAME
hyperfine \- command\-line benchmarking tool
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B hyperfine
.RB [ \-ihVN ]
.RB [ \-\-warmup
.IR NUM ]
.RB [ \-\-min\-runs
.IR NUM ]
.RB [ \-\-max\-runs
.IR NUM ]
.RB [ \-\-runs
.IR NUM ]
.RB [ \-\-setup
.IR CMD ]
.RB [ \-\-prepare
.IR CMD ]
.RB [ \-\-conclude
.IR CMD ]
.RB [ \-\-cleanup
.IR CMD ]
.RB [ \-\-parameter\-scan
.IR VAR
.IR MIN
.IR MAX ]
.RB [ \-\-parameter\-step\-size
.IR DELTA ]
.RB [ \-\-parameter\-list
.IR VAR
.IR VALUES ]
.RB [ \-\-shell
.IR SHELL ]
.RB [ \-\-style
.IR TYPE ]
.RB [ \-\-sort
.IR METHOD ]
.RB [ \-\-time-unit
.IR UNIT ]
.RB [ \-\-export\-asciidoc
.IR FILE ]
.RB [ \-\-export\-csv
.IR FILE ]
.RB [ \-\-export\-json
.IR FILE ]
.RB [ \-\-export\-markdown
.IR FILE ]
.RB [ \-\-export\-orgmode
.IR FILE ]
.RB [ \-\-output
.IR WHERE ]
.RB [ \-\-input
.IR WHERE ]
.RB [ \-\-command\-name
.IR NAME ]
.RI [ COMMAND... ]
.SH DESCRIPTION
A command\-line benchmarking tool which includes:
.LP
.RS
* Statistical analysis across multiple runs
.RE
.RS
* Support for arbitrary shell commands
.RE
.RS
* Constant feedback about the benchmark progress and current estimates
.RE
.RS
* Warmup runs can be executed before the actual benchmark
.RE
.RS
* Cache-clearing commands can be set up before each timing run
.RE
.RS
* Statistical outlier detection to detect interference from other programs and caching effects
.RE
.RS
* Export results to various formats: CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc
.RE
.RS
* Parameterized benchmarks (e.g. vary the number of threads)
.RE
.SH OPTIONS
.HP
\fB\-w\fR, \fB\-\-warmup\fR \fINUM\fP
.IP
Perform \fINUM\fP warmup runs before the actual benchmark. This can be used
to fill (disk) caches for I/O\-heavy programs.
.HP
\fB\-m\fR, \fB\-\-min\-runs\fR \fINUM\fP
.IP
Perform at least \fINUM\fP runs for each command. Default: 10.
.HP
\fB\-M\fR, \fB\-\-max\-runs\fR \fINUM\fP
.IP
Perform at most \fINUM\fP runs for each command. By default, there is no
limit.
.HP
\fB\-r\fR, \fB\-\-runs\fR \fINUM\fP
.IP
Perform exactly \fINUM\fP runs for each command. If this option is not specified,
\fBhyperfine\fR automatically determines the number of runs.
.HP
\fB\-s\fR, \fB\-\-setup\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP once before each set of timing runs. This is useful
for compiling your software or with the provided parameters, or to do any
other work that should happen once before a series of benchmark runs,
not every time as would happen with the \fB\-\-prepare\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-p\fR, \fB\-\-prepare\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP before each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk caches,
for example.
The \fB\-\-prepare\fR option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. In the latter case, each preparation command will be
run prior to the corresponding benchmark command.
.HP
\fB\-\-conclude\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP after each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk caches,
for example.
The \fB\-\-conclude\fR option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. In the latter case, each conclusion command will be
run after the corresponding benchmark command.
.HP
\fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-cleanup\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each individual
command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands to be benchmarked
produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up. It only runs once a series of
benchmark runs, as opposed to \fB\-\-conclude\fR option which runs after
every run.
.HP
\fB\-P\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-scan\fR \fIVAR\fP \fIMIN\fP \fIMAX\fP
.IP
Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range \fIMIN..MAX\fP. Replaces the
string '{\fIVAR\fP}' in each command by the current parameter value.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR threads 1 8 'make \-j {threads}'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'make \-j 1', 'make \-j 2', ..., 'make \-j 8'.
.IP
To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
arithmetics.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks with power of 2 increases: 'sleep 1', 'sleep
2', 'sleep 4', ...
.IP
The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
.HP
\fB\-D\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-step\-size\fR \fIDELTA\fP
.IP
This argument requires \fB\-\-parameter\-scan\fR to be specified as well. Traverse the
range \fIMIN..MAX\fP in steps of \fIDELTA\fP.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR delay 0.3 0.7 \fB\-D\fR 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
.HP
\fB\-L\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-list\fR \fIVAR\fP \fIVALUES\fP
.IP
Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma\-separated list of \fIVALUES\fP.
Replaces the string '{\fIVAR\fP}' in each command by the current parameter value.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-L\fR compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} \-O2 main.cpp'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'gcc \-O2 main.cpp' and 'clang \-O2 main.cpp'.
.IP
The option can be specified multiple times to run benchmarks for all
possible parameter combinations.
.HP
\fB\-S\fR, \fB\-\-shell\fR \fISHELL\fP
.IP
Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
like "bash \fB\-\-norc\fR". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be
executed directly. They can still have arguments, but more complex
things like "sleep 0.1; sleep 0.2" are not possible without a shell.
.HP
\fB\-N\fR
.IP
An alias for '\-\-shell=none'.
.HP
\fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-ignore\-failure\fR
.IP
Ignore non\-zero exit codes of the benchmarked programs.
.HP
\fB\-\-style\fR \fITYPE\fP
.IP
Set output style \fITYPE\fP (default: auto). Set this to 'basic' to disable output
coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable all effects even
if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to 'nocolor' to keep the
interactive output without any colors. Set this to 'color' to keep the colors
without any interactive output. Set this to 'none' to disable all the output
</output>

the given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit is always seconds.
.HP

.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given \fIFILE\fP.
The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-orgmode\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org\-mode table to the
given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-show\-output\fR
.IP
Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing it. This
will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it should only be
used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark output speed.
.HP
\fB\-\-output\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP and
apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
\-\-output=pipe.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Redirect output to \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP pipe
Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
.IP inherit
Don't redirect the output at all (same as \&'\-\-show\-output').
.IP "<FILE>"
Write the output to the given file.
.RE
.IP
This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the $HYPERFINE_ITERATION
environment variable: 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
.HP
\fB\-\-input\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Read from \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP "<FILE>"
Read the input from the given file.
.RE
.HP
\fB\-n\fR, \fB\-\-command\-name\fR \fiNAME\fP
.IP
Give a meaningful \fiNAME\fP to a command. This can be specified multiple times
if several commands are benchmarked.
.HP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
.IP
Print help
.HP
\fB\-V\fR, \fB\-\-version\fR
.IP
Print version
.SH EXAMPLES
.LP
Basic benchmark of 'find . -name todo.txt':
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR 'find . -name todo.txt'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Perform benchmarks for 'sleep 0.2' and 'sleep 3.2' with a minimum 5 runs each:

          to fill (disk) caches for I/O-heavy programs.
  -m, --min-runs <NUM>
          Perform at least NUM runs for each command (default: 10).
  -M, --max-runs <NUM>
          Perform at most NUM runs for each command. By default, there is no
          limit.
  -r, --runs <NUM>
          Perform exactly NUM runs for each command. If this option is not
          specified, hyperfine automatically determines the number of runs.
  -s, --setup <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each set of timing runs. This is useful for
          compiling your software with the provided parameters, or to do any
          other work that should happen once before a series of benchmark runs,
          not every time as would happen with the --prepare option.
      --reference <CMD>
          The reference command for the relative comparison of results. If this
          is unset, results are compared with the fastest command as reference.
      --reference-name <CMD>
          Give a meaningful name to the reference command.
  -p, --prepare <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk
          caches, for example.
          The --prepare option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          preparation command will be run prior to the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -C, --conclude <CMD>
          Execute CMD after each timing run. This is useful for killing
          long-running processes started (e.g. a web server started in
          --prepare), for example.
          The --conclude option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          conclude command will be run after the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -c, --cleanup <CMD>
          Execute CMD after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each
          individual command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands
          to be benchmarked produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up.
  -P, --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range MIN..MAX. Replaces
          the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current parameter value.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P threads 1 8 'make -j {threads}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'make -j 1', 'make -j 2', …, 'make -j 8'.
          
          To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
          arithmetics.
          
            Example: hyperfine -P size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
          
          This performs benchmarks with power of 2 increases: 'sleep 1', 'sleep
          2', 'sleep 4', …
          The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
  -D, --parameter-step-size <DELTA>
          This argument requires --parameter-scan to be specified as well.
          Traverse the range MIN..MAX in steps of DELTA.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
  -L, --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma-separated list
          VALUES. Replaces the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current
          parameter value.
          
          Example:  hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'gcc -O2 main.cpp' and 'clang -O2
          main.cpp'.
          
          The option can be specified multiple times to run benchmarks for all
          possible parameter combinations.
  -S, --shell <SHELL>
          Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
          the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
          like "bash --norc". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
          select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
          set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be
          executed directly. They can still have arguments, but more complex
          things like "sleep 0.1; sleep 0.2" are not possible without a shell.
  -N
          An alias for '--shell=none'.
  -i, --ignore-failure[=<MODE>]
          Ignore failures of the benchmarked programs. Without a value or with
          'all-non-zero', all non-zero exit codes are ignored. You can also
          provide a comma-separated list of exit codes to ignore (e.g.,
          --ignore-failure=1,2).
      --style <TYPE>
          Set output style type (default: auto). Set this to 'basic' to disable
          output coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable
          all effects even if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to
          'nocolor' to keep the interactive output without any colors. Set this
          to 'color' to keep the colors without any interactive output. Set this
          to 'none' to disable all the output of the tool.
      --sort <METHOD>
          Specify the sort order of the speed comparison summary and the
          exported tables for markup formats (Markdown, AsciiDoc, org-mode):
            * 'auto' (default): the speed comparison will be ordered by time and
              the markup tables will be ordered by command (input order).
            * 'command': order benchmarks in the way they were specified
            * 'mean-time': order benchmarks by mean runtime
  -u, --time-unit <UNIT>
          Set the time unit to be used. Possible values: microsecond,
          millisecond, second. If the option is not given, the time unit is
          determined automatically. This option affects the standard output as
          well as all export formats except for CSV and JSON.
      --export-asciidoc <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-csv <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given FILE. If you
          need the timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export
          format. The output time unit is always seconds.
      --export-json <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as
          JSON to the given FILE. The output time unit is always seconds
      --export-markdown <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-orgmode <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org-mode table to the
          given FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --show-output
          Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing
          it. This will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it
          should only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark
          output speed.
      --output <WHERE>
          Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
          some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is /dev/null and
          apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
          '--output=pipe'.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Redirect output to /dev/null (the default).
          
            pipe:     Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
          
            inherit:  Don't redirect the output at all (same as
            '--show-output').
          
            <FILE>:   Write the output to the given file.
          
          This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
          once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
          every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the
          '$HYPERFINE_ITERATION' environment variable:
              hyperfine 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
      --input <WHERE>
          Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Read from /dev/null (the default).
          
            <FILE>:   Read the input from the given file.
  -n, --command-name <NAME>
          Give a meaningful name to a command. This can be specified multiple
          times if several commands are benchmarked.
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
"""

LESS_THAN_WARNING = "Command took less than 5 ms to complete. Note that the results might be inaccurate because hyperfine can not calibrate the shell startup time much more precise than this limit. You can try to use the `-N`/`--shell=none` option to disable the shell completely."
OUTLIER_WARNING = "Statistical outliers were detected. Consider re-running this benchmark on a quiet system without any interferences from other programs. It might help to use the '--warmup' or '--prepare' options."
ZERO_COMPARISON_NOTE = "Note: The benchmark comparison could not be computed as some benchmark times are zero. This could be caused by background interference during the initial calibration phase of hyperfine, in combination with very fast commands (faster than a few milliseconds). Try to re-run the benchmark on a quiet system. If you did not do so already, try the --shell=none/-N option. If it does not help either, you command is most likely too fast to be accurately benchmarked by hyperfine."


def ansi(s, code, color_enabled):
    return f"\033[{code}m{s}\033[0m" if color_enabled else s


def os_error_text(exc):
    eno = getattr(exc, "errno", None)
    if eno is None:
        return str(exc)
    return f"{os.strerror(eno)} (os error {eno})"


def clap_error(message, usage=None, tip=None):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {message}\n")
    if tip:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\n  tip: {tip}\n")
    if usage:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\nUsage: {usage}\n")
    sys.stderr.write("\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def runtime_error(message):
    sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {message}\n")
    sys.exit(1)


@dataclass
class Options:
    warmup: int = 0
    min_runs: int = 10
    min_runs_explicit: bool = False
    max_runs: int | None = None
    runs: int | None = None

    setup_seen: bool = False
    reference: str | None = None
    reference_name: str | None = None
    prepare: list = field(default_factory=list)
    conclude: list = field(default_factory=list)
    cleanup: str | None = None
    cleanup_seen: bool = False
    parameter_scan: tuple | None = None
    parameter_step: str | None = None
    parameter_lists: list = field(default_factory=list)

    ignore_failure: object = None  # None, 'all', or set[int]

def option_display(long):
    mapping = {
        "warmup": "--warmup", "runs": "--runs", "min-runs": "--min-runs", "max-runs": "--max-runs",
        "ignore-failure": "--ignore-failure", "parameter-step-size": "--parameter-step-size",
    }
    return mapping.get(long, f"--{long}")


def parse_uint(s, optlong):
    try:
        if s.startswith("-"):
            raise ValueError
        # Rust's unsigned integer parser rejects leading plus signs too.
        if not s or any(ch < '0' or ch > '9' for ch in s):
            raise ValueError
        return int(s, 10)
    except Exception:
        runtime_error(f"Could not read numeric integer argument to '{option_display(optlong)}': invalid digit found in string")


def parse_ignore_value(val):
    if val is None or val == "" or val == "all-non-zero":
        return "all"
    codes = set()
    for part in val.split(','):
        try:
            if not part or part.startswith('-') or any(ch < '0' or ch > '9' for ch in part):
                raise ValueError
            codes.add(int(part, 10))
        except Exception:
            runtime_error("Could not read numeric integer argument to '--ignore-failure': invalid digit found in string")
    return codes


LONG_VALUE_COUNTS = {
    "warmup": 1, "min-runs": 1, "max-runs": 1, "runs": 1, "setup": 1,
    "reference": 1, "reference-name": 1, "prepare": 1, "conclude": 1, "cleanup": 1,
    "parameter-scan": 3, "parameter-step-size": 1, "parameter-list": 2,
    "shell": 1, "style": 1, "sort": 1, "time-unit": 1,
    "export-asciidoc": 1, "export-csv": 1, "export-json": 1, "export-markdown": 1,
    "export-orgmode": 1, "output": 1, "input": 1, "command-name": 1,
}
LONG_FLAGS = {"help", "version", "show-output"}
SHORT_MAP = {
    'w': ("warmup", 1), 'm': ("min-runs", 1), 'M': ("max-runs", 1), 'r': ("runs", 1),
    's': ("setup", 1), 'p': ("prepare", 1), 'C': ("conclude", 1), 'c': ("cleanup", 1),
    'P': ("parameter-scan", 3), 'D': ("parameter-step-size", 1), 'L': ("parameter-list", 2),
    'S': ("shell", 1), 'u': ("time-unit", 1), 'n': ("command-name", 1),
    'N': ("N", 0), 'i': ("ignore-failure", 0), 'h': ("help", 0), 'V': ("version", 0),

LONG_DISPLAY = {
    "warmup": "--warmup <NUM>", "min-runs": "--min-runs <NUM>", "max-runs": "--max-runs <NUM>",
    "runs": "--runs <NUM>", "setup": "--setup <CMD>", "reference": "--reference <CMD>",
    "reference-name": "--reference-name <CMD>", "prepare": "--prepare <CMD>", "conclude": "--conclude <CMD>",
    "cleanup": "--cleanup <CMD>", "parameter-scan": "--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>",

def missing_value(opt, count, got=0):
    disp = LONG_DISPLAY.get(opt, f"--{opt}")
    if count == 1:
        clap_error(f"a value is required for '{disp}' but none was supplied")
    else:
        noun = "was" if got == 1 else "were"
        clap_error(f"{count} values required for '{disp}' but {got} {noun} provided", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")


def apply_option(opts, name, vals, explicit_style=False):
    if name == "warmup":
        opts.warmup = parse_uint(vals[0], name)
    elif name == "min-runs":
        opts.min_runs = parse_uint(vals[0], name); opts.min_runs_explicit = True
    elif name == "max-runs":
        opts.max_runs = parse_uint(vals[0], name)
    elif name == "runs":
        opts.runs = parse_uint(vals[0], name)
    elif name == "setup":
        if opts.setup_seen:
            clap_error("the argument '--setup <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        opts.setup = vals[0]; opts.setup_seen = True
    elif name == "reference":
        opts.reference = vals[0]
    elif name == "reference-name":
        opts.reference_name = vals[0]
    elif name == "prepare":
        opts.prepare.append(vals[0])
    elif name == "conclude":
        opts.conclude.append(vals[0])
    elif name == "cleanup":
        if opts.cleanup_seen:
            clap_error("the argument '--cleanup <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        opts.cleanup = vals[0]; opts.cleanup_seen = True
    elif name == "parameter-scan":
        if opts.parameter_scan is not None:
            clap_error("the argument '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        opts.parameter_scan = (vals[0], vals[1], vals[2])
    elif name == "parameter-step-size":
        opts.parameter_step = vals[0]
    elif name == "parameter-list":
        opts.parameter_lists.append((vals[0], vals[1]))
    elif name == "shell":
        opts.shell = vals[0]
    elif name == "N":
        opts.shell = "none"
    elif name == "ignore-failure":
        opts.ignore_failure = parse_ignore_value(vals[0] if vals else None)
    elif name == "style":
        if opts.style_explicit:
            clap_error("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        val = vals[0]
        if val not in ["auto", "basic", "full", "nocolor", "color", "none"]:
            clap_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--style <TYPE>'\n  [possible values: auto, basic, full, nocolor, color, none]")
        opts.style = val; opts.style_explicit = True
    elif name == "sort":
        val = vals[0]
        if val not in ["auto", "command", "mean-time"]:
            clap_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--sort <METHOD>'\n  [possible values: auto, command, mean-time]")
        opts.sort = val
    elif name == "time-unit":
        val = vals[0]
        if val not in ["microsecond", "millisecond", "second"]:
            msg = f"invalid value '{val}' for '--time-unit <UNIT>'\n  [possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second]"
            if val == "ms":
                msg += "\n\n  tip: a similar value exists: 'millisecond'"
            elif val == "s":
                msg += "\n\n  tip: a similar value exists: 'second'"
            clap_error(msg)
        opts.time_unit = val
    elif name == "export-asciidoc": opts.export_asciidoc = vals[0]
    elif name == "export-csv": opts.export_csv = vals[0]
    elif name == "export-json": opts.export_json = vals[0]
    elif name == "export-markdown": opts.export_markdown = vals[0]
    elif name == "export-orgmode": opts.export_orgmode = vals[0]
    elif name == "show-output": opts.show_output = True
    elif name == "output": opts.output.append(vals[0])
    elif name == "input":
        if opts.input_seen:
            clap_error("the argument '--input <WHERE>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        opts.input = vals[0]; opts.input_seen = True
    elif name == "command-name": opts.command_names.append(vals[0])


def first_help_or_version(argv):
    # clap's help/version action fires as soon as that flag is encountered.
    for arg in argv:
        if arg == "--":
            break
        if arg == "--help" or arg == "-h":
            return "help"
        if arg == "--version" or arg == "-V":
            return "version"
        if arg.startswith("-") and not arg.startswith("--") and len(arg) > 2:
            # grouped short flags: -Vh prints version, -hV prints help.
            for ch in arg[1:]:
                if ch == '=':
                    break
                if ch == 'h':
                    return "help"
                if ch == 'V':
                    return "version"
                # stop scanning a cluster when an option with an attached value begins
                if ch in SHORT_MAP and SHORT_MAP[ch][1] > 0:
                    break
    return None


def parse_args(argv):
    early = first_help_or_version(argv)
    if early == "help":
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        sys.exit(0)
    if early == "version":
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n")
        sys.exit(0)

    opts = Options()
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            opts.commands.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        if arg.startswith("--") and len(arg) > 2:
            body = arg[2:]
            if "=" in body:
                name, eqval = body.split("=", 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, eqval, has_eq = body, None, False
            if name in LONG_FLAGS:
                apply_option(opts, name, [])
                i += 1
                continue
            if name == "ignore-failure":
                if has_eq:
                    apply_option(opts, name, [eqval])
                else:
                    apply_option(opts, name, [])
                i += 1
                continue
            if name not in LONG_VALUE_COUNTS:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '--{name}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
            cnt = LONG_VALUE_COUNTS[name]
            vals = []
            if has_eq:
                vals.append(eqval)
                if cnt > 1:
                    needed = cnt - 1
                    if i + needed >= len(argv):
                        missing_value(name, cnt, len(vals) + max(0, len(argv)-i-1))
                    vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+needed])
                    i += needed
            else:
                if i + cnt >= len(argv):
                    got = max(0, len(argv) - i - 1)
                    missing_value(name, cnt, got)
                # Negative-looking values are treated by clap as arguments/options for integer options in many cases.
                if cnt == 1 and argv[i+1].startswith('-') and name in {"runs", "warmup", "min-runs", "max-runs"}:
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{argv[i+1]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{argv[i+1]}' as a value, use '-- {argv[i+1]}'")
                vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+cnt])
                i += cnt
            apply_option(opts, name, vals)
            i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            cluster = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            consumed_next = 0
            while j < len(cluster):
                ch = cluster[j]
                if ch == '=':
                    # e.g. -i=1 is handled when i sees the = rest.
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '-{cluster[j:]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
                if ch not in SHORT_MAP:
                    bad = "-" + cluster[j:]
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{bad}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{bad}' as a value, use '-- {bad}'" if bad[1:].lstrip('-').isdigit() else None)
                name, cnt = SHORT_MAP[ch]
                if cnt == 0:
                    if name == "ignore-failure" and j + 1 < len(cluster) and cluster[j+1] == '=':
                        apply_option(opts, name, [cluster[j+2:]])
                        j = len(cluster)
                        continue
                    apply_option(opts, name, [])
                    j += 1
                    continue
                # value option: rest of cluster is first value, unless empty.
                vals = []
                rest = cluster[j+1:]
                if rest:
                    vals.append(rest)
                    if cnt > 1:
                        need = cnt - 1
                        if i + need >= len(argv):
                            missing_value(name, cnt, len(vals) + max(0, len(argv)-i-1))
                        vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+need])
                        consumed_next = need
                    j = len(cluster)
                else:
                    if i + cnt >= len(argv):
                        got = max(0, len(argv)-i-1)
                        missing_value(name, cnt, got)
                    if cnt == 1 and argv[i+1].startswith('-') and name in {"runs", "warmup", "min-runs", "max-runs", "parameter-step-size"}:
                        clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{argv[i+1]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{argv[i+1]}' as a value, use '-- {argv[i+1]}'")
                    vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+cnt])
                    consumed_next = cnt
                    j = len(cluster)
                apply_option(opts, name, vals)
            i += 1 + consumed_next
        else:
            opts.commands.append(arg)
            i += 1
    return opts


def color_enabled(opts):
    return opts.style in ("color", "full")


def stdout_enabled(opts):
    return opts.style != "none"


def subst(template, params):
    s = template
    for k, v in params.items():
        s = s.replace("{" + k + "}", v)
    return s


def parse_decimal(s):
    try:
        return Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        runtime_error("Error while parsing parameter scan arguments (Invalid decimal: unknown character)")


def decimal_is_integral_string(s):
    return "." not in s and "e" not in s.lower()


def parameter_scan_values(var, min_s, max_s, step_s):
    lo = parse_decimal(min_s)
    hi = parse_decimal(max_s)
    if lo > hi:
        runtime_error("Empty parameter range")
    if step_s is None:
        if not decimal_is_integral_string(min_s) or not decimal_is_integral_string(max_s):
            runtime_error("A step size is required when the range bounds are floating point numbers. The step size can be specified with the '-D/--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' parameter")
        step = Decimal(1)
    else:
        step = parse_decimal(step_s)
        if step == 0:
            runtime_error("Zero is not a valid parameter step")
        if step < 0:
            runtime_error("Parameter range is too large")
    vals = []
    x = lo
    count = 0
    # Include the upper bound. Guard against huge/infinite ranges.
    while x <= hi:
        vals.append(str(x))
        x = x + step
        count += 1
        if count > 1000000:
            runtime_error("Parameter range is too large")
    if not vals:
        runtime_error("Empty parameter range")
    return vals


def parameter_combinations(opts):
    if opts.parameter_scan is not None and opts.parameter_lists:
        # Error text depends on which appeared first; this is close enough for normal use.
        clap_error("the argument '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' cannot be used with '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>'", "executable --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX> <command>...")
    if opts.parameter_step is not None and opts.parameter_scan is None:
        clap_error("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>", "executable --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX> --parameter-step-size <DELTA> <command>...")
    if opts.parameter_scan is not None:
        var, lo, hi = opts.parameter_scan
        vals = parameter_scan_values(var, lo, hi, opts.parameter_step)
        return [{var: v} for v in vals], True
    if opts.parameter_lists:
        combos = [dict()]
        for var, values in opts.parameter_lists:
            vals = values.split(',')
            new = []
            for val in vals:
                for combo in combos:
                    c = dict(combo)
                    c[var] = val
                    new.append(c)
            combos = new
        return combos, True
    return [dict()], False


@dataclass
class Benchmark:
    command: str
    display: str
    params: dict
    user_index: int | None = None
    is_reference: bool = False


def build_benchmarks(opts):
    combos, has_params = parameter_combinations(opts)
    user_total = len(combos) * len(opts.commands)
    n_names = len(opts.command_names)
    if n_names:
        if n_names == 1:
            pass
        elif n_names == user_total:
            pass
        elif n_names > user_total:
            runtime_error(f"Too many --command-name options: Expected {user_total} at most")
        else:
            runtime_error(f"'--command-name' has been specified {n_names} times. It has to appear exactly once, or exactly {user_total} times (number of benchmarks)")
    benches = []
    if opts.reference is not None:
        benches.append(Benchmark(opts.reference, opts.reference_name or opts.reference, {}, None, True))
    seq = 0
    for combo in combos:
        for cmd_i, cmd in enumerate(opts.commands):
            command = subst(cmd, combo)
            display = command
            if n_names == 1:
                if has_params:
                    display = subst(opts.command_names[0], combo)
                elif cmd_i == 0:
                    display = subst(opts.command_names[0], combo)
            elif n_names == user_total:
                display = subst(opts.command_names[seq], combo)
            benches.append(Benchmark(command, display, combo, seq, False))
            seq += 1
    return benches, user_total


def validate(opts, benches, user_total):
    if not opts.commands:
        # Include only the compact usage for the common case.
        usage = "executable <command>..."
        sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <command>...\n\n")
        sys.stderr.write(f"Usage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    if opts.style_explicit and opts.show_output:
        clap_error("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used with '--show-output'", "executable --style <TYPE> <command>...")
    if opts.show_output and opts.output:
        clap_error("the argument '--show-output' cannot be used with '--output <WHERE>'", "executable --show-output <command>...")
    if opts.runs is not None and opts.min_runs_explicit:
        clap_error("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--min-runs <NUM>'", "executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")
    if opts.runs is not None and opts.max_runs is not None:
        clap_error("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--max-runs <NUM>'", "executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")
    if opts.max_runs is not None and opts.min_runs_explicit and opts.min_runs > opts.max_runs:
        runtime_error("Conflicting requirements for the number of runs (empty range, min is larger than max)")
    if opts.reference_name is not None and opts.reference is None:
        clap_error("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --reference <CMD>", "executable --reference <CMD> --reference-name <CMD> <command>...")
    total = len(benches)
    for optname, values in (("--prepare", opts.prepare), ("--conclude", opts.conclude), ("--output", opts.output)):
        if values and len(values) not in (1, total):
            runtime_error(f"The '{optname}' option has to be provided just once or N times, where N={total} is the number of benchmark commands (including a potential reference).")
    if opts.input != "null" and not os.path.exists(opts.input):
        runtime_error(f"The file '{opts.input}' specified as '--input' does not exist")
    # Preflight export files, matching hyperfine's early export-file errors.
    for path in [opts.export_asciidoc, opts.export_csv, opts.export_json, opts.export_markdown, opts.export_orgmode]:
        if path:
            try:
                with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8"):
                    pass
            except OSError as e:
                runtime_error(f"Could not create export file '{path}': {os_error_text(e)}")


def shell_argv(opts, cmd):
    if opts.shell == "none":
        try:
            return shlex.split(cmd)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ParseCommandError(str(e))
    shell = opts.shell
    if shell == "default":
        parts = ["/bin/sh"]
    else:
        try:
            parts = shlex.split(shell)
        except ValueError:
            parts = [shell]
    return parts + ["-c", cmd]


class ParseCommandError(Exception):
    pass


def calibrate_shell(opts):
    if opts.shell == "none":
        return 0.0
    shell = opts.shell
    if shell == "default":
        parts = ["/bin/sh"]
        display = "/bin/sh"
    else:
        try:
            parts = shlex.split(shell)
        except ValueError:
            parts = [shell]
        display = shell
    argv = parts + ["-c", ""]
    samples = []
    for _ in range(3):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            cp = subprocess.run(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        except OSError:
            runtime_error(f"Could not measure shell execution time. Make sure you can run '{display} -c \"\"'.")
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            runtime_error(f"Could not measure shell execution time. Make sure you can run '{display} -c \"\"'.")
        samples.append(elapsed)
    return min(samples) if samples else 0.0


def open_stdio(input_spec, output_spec):
    handles = []
    # stdin
    try:
        if input_spec == "null":
            stdin = open(os.devnull, "rb")
            handles.append(stdin)
        else:
            stdin = open(input_spec, "rb")
            handles.append(stdin)
        # stdout/stderr
        if output_spec == "inherit":
            stdout = None
            stderr = None
        elif output_spec == "pipe":
            stdout = subprocess.PIPE
            stderr = open(os.devnull, "wb")
            handles.append(stderr)
        elif output_spec == "null":
            stdout = open(os.devnull, "wb")
            stderr = open(os.devnull, "wb")
            handles += [stdout, stderr]
        else:
            stdout = open(output_spec, "wb")
            stderr = open(os.devnull, "wb")
            handles += [stdout, stderr]
    except OSError:
        for h in handles:
            try: h.close()
            except Exception: pass
        raise
    return stdin, stdout, stderr, handles


def run_external(opts, cmd, env_extra=None, output_spec="null", calibration=0.0, timed=True):
    try:
        argv = shell_argv(opts, cmd)
    except ParseCommandError as e:
        raise
    if not argv:
        # Empty command without a shell cannot be spawned.
        raise OSError(2, os.strerror(2))
    env = os.environ.copy()
    if env_extra:
        env.update(env_extra)
    stdin = stdout = stderr = None
    handles = []
    try:
        stdin, stdout, stderr, handles = open_stdio(opts.input, output_spec)
        before = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            p = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=stdin, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr, env=env)
        except OSError:
            raise
        if stdout == subprocess.PIPE:
            p.communicate()
            rc = p.returncode
        else:
            rc = p.wait()
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        after = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    finally:
        for h in handles:
            try:
                h.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
    if rc is not None and rc < 0:
        # Shells report signal exits as 128+signum; direct execution in Rust often surfaces this too.
        rc_display = 128 + (-rc)
    else:
        rc_display = int(rc or 0)
    elapsed_adj = max(0.0, elapsed - (calibration if timed and opts.shell != "none" else 0.0))
    user = max(0.0, after.ru_utime - before.ru_utime)
    system = max(0.0, after.ru_stime - before.ru_stime)
    mem = max(0, int(after.ru_maxrss) * 1024)
    return rc_display, elapsed_adj, user, system, mem


def failure_is_ignored(opts, code):
    if code == 0:
        return True
    if opts.ignore_failure == "all":
        return True
    if isinstance(opts.ignore_failure, set) and code in opts.ignore_failure:
        return True
    return False


@dataclass
class Result:
    benchmark: Benchmark
    times: list
    users: list
    systems: list
    memories: list
    exit_codes: list
    mean: float
    stddev: float | None
    median: float
    min: float
    max: float
    user: float
    system: float
    ignored_nonzero: bool = False


def compute_result(bench, times, users, systems, mems, codes, ignored):
    mean = sum(times)/len(times) if times else 0.0
    std = statistics.stdev(times) if len(times) >= 2 else None
    med = statistics.median(times) if times else 0.0
    return Result(bench, times, users, systems, mems, codes, mean, std, med,
                  min(times) if times else 0.0, max(times) if times else 0.0,
                  sum(users)/len(users) if users else 0.0,
                  sum(systems)/len(systems) if systems else 0.0,
                  ignored)


def unit_info(unit):
    if unit == "microsecond":
        return 1_000_000.0, "µs", 1
    if unit == "millisecond":
        return 1_000.0, "ms", 1
    if unit == "second":
        return 1.0, "s", 3
    raise ValueError(unit)


def choose_unit(seconds, forced=None):
    if forced:
        return forced
    if seconds < 0.001:
        return "microsecond"
    if seconds < 1.0:
        return "millisecond"
    return "second"


def fmt_time(seconds, unit, width=0):
    factor, label, dec = unit_info(unit)
    val = seconds * factor
    s = f"{val:.{dec}f} {label}"
    if width:
        return f"{s:>{width}}"
    return s


def fmt_time_no_unit(seconds, unit):
    factor, label, dec = unit_info(unit)
    return f"{seconds*factor:.{dec}f}"


def print_tool(opts, s=""):
    if stdout_enabled(opts):
        print(s)


def write_stdout(opts, s):
    if stdout_enabled(opts):
        sys.stdout.write(s)
        sys.stdout.flush()


def warn(opts, msg):
    c = color_enabled(opts)
    label = ansi("Warning", "33", c)
    sys.stderr.write(f" \n  {label}: {msg}\n")
    sys.stderr.flush()


def print_benchmark_header(opts, index, display):
    c = color_enabled(opts)
    if c:
        line = f"{ansi('Benchmark ', '1', True)}{ansi(str(index), '1', True)}: {display}"
    else:
        line = f"Benchmark {index}: {display}"
    print_tool(opts, line)


def print_result(opts, res):
    unit = choose_unit(res.mean, opts.time_unit)
    c = color_enabled(opts)
    if len(res.times) == 1:
        label = ansi("abs", "1;32", c)
        val = fmt_time(res.mean, unit, 12)
        if c: val = ansi(val, "1;32", True)
        user_s = fmt_time(res.user, unit)
        sys_s = fmt_time(res.system, unit)
        if c:
            user_s = ansi(user_s, "34", True); sys_s = ansi(sys_s, "34", True)
        print_tool(opts, f"  Time ({label} ≡): {val}               [User: {user_s}, System: {sys_s}]")
    else:
        label = ansi("mean", "1;32", c)
        mean_s = fmt_time(res.mean, unit, 12)
        std_s = fmt_time(res.stddev or 0.0, unit, 8)
        if c:
            mean_s = ansi(mean_s, "1;32", True)
        user_s = fmt_time(res.user, unit); sys_s = fmt_time(res.system, unit)
        if c:
            user_s = ansi(user_s, "34", True); sys_s = ansi(sys_s, "34", True)
        print_tool(opts, f"  Time ({label} ± σ): {mean_s} ± {std_s}    [User: {user_s}, System: {sys_s}]")
        min_s = fmt_time(res.min, unit, 12)
        max_s = fmt_time(res.max, unit, 8)
        print_tool(opts, f"  Range (min … max): {min_s} … {max_s}    {len(res.times)} runs")
    print_tool(opts, " ")


def nth_error_context(kind, iteration):
    if kind == "warmup":
        return f"warmup iteration {iteration}"
    if iteration == 0:
        return "the first benchmark run"
    return f"benchmark iteration {iteration}"


def command_failure_error(code, context):
    runtime_error(f"Command terminated with non-zero exit code {code} in {context}. Use the '-i'/'--ignore-failure' option if you want to ignore this. Alternatively, use the '--show-output' option to debug what went wrong.")


def lifecycle_failure_error(kind):
    labels = {"setup": "setup", "prepare": "preparation", "conclude": "conclusion", "cleanup": "cleanup"}
    runtime_error(f"The {labels[kind]} command terminated with a non-zero exit code. Append ' || true' to the command if you are sure that this can be ignored.")


def select_list_value(values, index, total, bench):
    if not values:
        return None
    if len(values) == 1:
        return subst(values[0], bench.params)
    return subst(values[index], bench.params)


def output_for_benchmark(opts, index, bench):
    if opts.show_output:
        return "inherit"
    if not opts.output:
        return "null"
    if len(opts.output) == 1:
        return subst(opts.output[0], bench.params)
    return subst(opts.output[index], bench.params)


def run_lifecycle(opts, kind, cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration):
    if not cmd:
        return
    cmd = subst(cmd, bench.params)
    try:
        code, *_ = run_external(opts, cmd, {}, output_spec, calibration, timed=False)
    except ParseCommandError:
        lifecycle_failure_error(kind)
    except OSError:
        lifecycle_failure_error(kind)
    if code != 0:
        lifecycle_failure_error(kind)


def run_benchmark(opts, bench, bench_index, total, calibration):
    output_spec = output_for_benchmark(opts, bench_index, bench)
    setup_cmd = subst(opts.setup, bench.params) if opts.setup else None
    cleanup_cmd = subst(opts.cleanup, bench.params) if opts.cleanup else None
    prepare_cmd = select_list_value(opts.prepare, bench_index, total, bench)
    conclude_cmd = select_list_value(opts.conclude, bench_index, total, bench)

    print_benchmark_header(opts, bench_index + 1, bench.display)

    if opts.runs == 0:
        # Match the upstream bug/behavior: print the benchmark header and never finish.
        while True:
            time.sleep(3600)

    run_lifecycle(opts, "setup", setup_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)

    # Warmup runs
    for wi in range(opts.warmup):
        run_lifecycle(opts, "prepare", prepare_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)
        try:
            code, _, _, _, _ = run_external(opts, bench.command, {"HYPERFINE_ITERATION": f"warmup-{wi}"}, output_spec, calibration, timed=False)
        except ParseCommandError as e:
            runtime_error(f"Failed to parse command '{bench.command}': {e}")
        except OSError as e:
            runtime_error(f"Failed to run command '{bench.command}': {os_error_text(e)}")
        if code != 0 and not failure_is_ignored(opts, code):
            command_failure_error(code, nth_error_context("warmup", wi))
        run_lifecycle(opts, "conclude", conclude_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)

    times = []; users = []; systems = []; mems = []; codes = []
    ignored_nonzero = False
    target_min = opts.min_runs
    if opts.max_runs is not None and not opts.min_runs_explicit:
        target_min = min(target_min, opts.max_runs)
    exact = opts.runs
    iteration = 0
    total_measured = 0.0
    while True:
        if exact is not None:
            if iteration >= exact:
                break
        else:
            if iteration >= target_min and total_measured >= 3.0:
                break
            if opts.max_runs is not None and iteration >= opts.max_runs:
                break
        run_lifecycle(opts, "prepare", prepare_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)
        try:
            code, elapsed, user, system, mem = run_external(opts, bench.command, {"HYPERFINE_ITERATION": str(iteration)}, output_spec, calibration, timed=True)
        except ParseCommandError as e:
            runtime_error(f"Failed to parse command '{bench.command}': {e}")
        except OSError as e:
            runtime_error(f"Failed to run command '{bench.command}': {os_error_text(e)}")
        if code != 0:
            if failure_is_ignored(opts, code):
                ignored_nonzero = True
            else:
                command_failure_error(code, nth_error_context("benchmark", iteration))
        times.append(elapsed); users.append(user); systems.append(system); mems.append(mem); codes.append(code)
        total_measured += elapsed
        run_lifecycle(opts, "conclude", conclude_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)
        iteration += 1
    res = compute_result(bench, times, users, systems, mems, codes, ignored_nonzero)
    print_result(opts, res)
    if opts.shell != "none" and res.mean < 0.005:
        warn(opts, LESS_THAN_WARNING)
    if res.ignored_nonzero:
        warn(opts, "Ignoring non-zero exit code.")
    # Simple outlier warning approximation: only for highly skewed samples; avoids noisy snapshots.
    if len(res.times) >= 10 and res.stddev and res.mean > 0 and res.stddev / res.mean > 1.0:
        warn(opts, OUTLIER_WARNING)
    run_lifecycle(opts, "cleanup", cleanup_cmd, bench, output_spec, calibration)
    return res


def relative_uncertainty(ref, other, ratio):
    a = (ref.stddev or 0.0) / ref.mean if ref.mean else 0.0
    b = (other.stddev or 0.0) / other.mean if other.mean else 0.0
    return ratio * math.sqrt(a*a + b*b)


def print_summary(opts, results):
    if len(results) <= 1:
        return
    if any(r.mean == 0 for r in results):
        sys.stderr.write(ZERO_COMPARISON_NOTE + "\n")
        return
    if opts.reference is not None:
        ref = results[0]
    else:
        ref = min(results, key=lambda r: r.mean)
    if opts.sort == "command":
        print_tool(opts, "Relative speed comparison")
        for r in results:
            ratio = r.mean / ref.mean
            if r is ref:
                print_tool(opts, f"        {1.00:0.2f}          {r.benchmark.display}")
            else:
                unc = relative_uncertainty(ref, r, ratio)
                print_tool(opts, f"        {ratio:0.2f} ±  {unc:0.2f}  {r.benchmark.display}")
        return
    ordered = sorted([r for r in results if r is not ref], key=lambda r: r.mean)
    print_tool(opts, "Summary")
    print_tool(opts, f"  {ref.benchmark.display} ran")
    for r in ordered:
        if r.mean >= ref.mean:
            ratio = r.mean / ref.mean
            unc = relative_uncertainty(ref, r, ratio)
            print_tool(opts, f"    {ratio:.2f} ± {unc:.2f} times faster than {r.benchmark.display}")
        else:
            ratio = ref.mean / r.mean
            unc = relative_uncertainty(r, ref, ratio)
            print_tool(opts, f"    {ratio:.2f} ± {unc:.2f} times slower than {r.benchmark.display}")


def export_unit(opts, results):
    if opts.time_unit:
        return opts.time_unit
    if not results:
        return "second"
    ref = min(results, key=lambda r: r.mean)
    return choose_unit(ref.mean, None)


def relative_values(results, opts):
    if not results or any(r.mean == 0 for r in results):
        return {r: None for r in results}
    ref = results[0] if opts.reference is not None else min(results, key=lambda r: r.mean)
    vals = {}
    for r in results:
        ratio = r.mean / ref.mean
        unc = relative_uncertainty(ref, r, ratio)
        vals[id(r)] = (ratio, unc, r is ref)
    return vals


def format_relative(r, rels):
    val = rels.get(id(r))
    if val is None:
        return "N/A"
    ratio, unc, is_ref = val
    if is_ref:
        return "1.00"
    return f"{ratio:.2f} ± {unc:.2f}"


def escape_md(s):
    return s.replace("|", "\\|")


def sorted_for_markup(results, opts):
    if opts.sort == "mean-time":
        return sorted(results, key=lambda r: r.mean)
    return list(results)


def write_json(path, results):
    data = {"results": []}
    for r in results:
        data["results"].append({
            "command": r.benchmark.display,
            "mean": r.mean,
            "stddev": r.stddev,
            "median": r.median,
            "user": r.user,
            "system": r.system,
            "min": r.min,
            "max": r.max,
            "times": r.times,
            "memory_usage_byte": r.memories,
            "exit_codes": r.exit_codes,
        })
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")


def float_csv(x):
    if x is None:
        return "0"
    if x == 0:
        return "0"
    return repr(float(x))


def write_csv_export(path, results):
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["command", "mean", "stddev", "median", "user", "system", "min", "max"])
        for r in results:
            w.writerow([r.benchmark.display, float_csv(r.mean), float_csv(r.stddev), float_csv(r.median), float_csv(r.user), float_csv(r.system), float_csv(r.min), float_csv(r.max)])


def mean_cell(r, unit):
    if r.stddev is None:
        return fmt_time_no_unit(r.mean, unit)
    return f"{fmt_time_no_unit(r.mean, unit)} ± {fmt_time_no_unit(r.stddev, unit)}"


def write_markdown(path, results, opts):
    unit = export_unit(opts, results)
    _, label, _ = unit_info(unit)
    rels = relative_values(results, opts)
    rows = sorted_for_markup(results, opts)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"| Command | Mean [{label}] | Min [{label}] | Max [{label}] | Relative |\n")
        f.write("|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n")
        for r in rows:
            cmd = escape_md(r.benchmark.display)
            f.write(f"| `{cmd}` | {mean_cell(r, unit)} | {fmt_time_no_unit(r.min, unit)} | {fmt_time_no_unit(r.max, unit)} | {format_relative(r, rels)} |\n")


def write_asciidoc(path, results, opts):
    unit = export_unit(opts, results)
    _, label, _ = unit_info(unit)
    rels = relative_values(results, opts)
    rows = sorted_for_markup(results, opts)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write('[cols="<,>,>,>,>"]\n|===\n')
        for h in ["Command", f"Mean [{label}]", f"Min [{label}]", f"Max [{label}]", "Relative"]:
            f.write(f"| {h} \n")
        f.write("\n")
        for r in rows:
            cmd = escape_md(r.benchmark.display)
            vals = [f"`{cmd}`", mean_cell(r, unit), fmt_time_no_unit(r.min, unit), fmt_time_no_unit(r.max, unit), format_relative(r, rels)]
            for v in vals:
                f.write(f"| {v} \n")
            # hyperfine leaves a blank-looking separator line after each row except the final marker follows directly after last cell newline.
        f.write("|===")


def write_orgmode(path, results, opts):
    unit = export_unit(opts, results)
    _, label, _ = unit_info(unit)
    rels = relative_values(results, opts)
    rows = sorted_for_markup(results, opts)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"| Command  |  Mean [{label}] |  Min [{label}] |  Max [{label}] |  Relative |\n")
        f.write("|--+--+--+--+--|\n")
        for r in rows:
            cmd = escape_md(r.benchmark.display)
            f.write(f"| ={cmd}=  |  {mean_cell(r, unit)} |  {fmt_time_no_unit(r.min, unit)} |  {fmt_time_no_unit(r.max, unit)} |  {format_relative(r, rels)} |\n")


def perform_exports(opts, results):
    if opts.export_json:
        write_json(opts.export_json, results)
    if opts.export_csv:
        write_csv_export(opts.export_csv, results)
    if opts.export_markdown:
        write_markdown(opts.export_markdown, results, opts)
    if opts.export_asciidoc:
        write_asciidoc(opts.export_asciidoc, results, opts)
    if opts.export_orgmode:
        write_orgmode(opts.export_orgmode, results, opts)


def main(argv):
    opts = parse_args(argv)
    # Build benchmarks before validation that depends on expanded counts.
    benches, user_total = build_benchmarks(opts)
    validate(opts, benches, user_total)
    calibration = calibrate_shell(opts)
    results = []
    total = len(benches)
    for idx, bench in enumerate(benches):
        res = run_benchmark(opts, bench, idx, total, calibration)
        results.append(res)
    print_summary(opts, results)
    perform_exports(opts, results)

    try:
        main(sys.argv[1:])
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        # Rust/clap tools typically just terminate on Ctrl-C; use conventional status.

def first_help_or_version(argv):
    # clap's help/version action fires as soon as that flag is encountered.
    for arg in argv:
        if arg == "--":
            break
        if arg == "--help" or arg == "-h":
            return "help"
        if arg == "--version" or arg == "-V":
            return "version"
        if arg.startswith("-") and not arg.startswith("--") and len(arg) > 2:
            # grouped short flags: -Vh prints version, -hV prints help.
            for ch in arg[1:]:
                if ch == '=':
                    break
                if ch == 'h':
                    return "help"
                if ch == 'V':
                    return "version"
                # stop scanning a cluster when an option with an attached value begins
                if ch in SHORT_MAP and SHORT_MAP[ch][1] > 0:
                    break
    return None


def parse_args(argv):
    early = first_help_or_version(argv)
    if early == "help":
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        sys.exit(0)
    if early == "version":
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n")
        sys.exit(0)

    opts = Options()
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            opts.commands.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        if arg.startswith("--") and len(arg) > 2:
            body = arg[2:]
            if "=" in body:
                name, eqval = body.split("=", 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, eqval, has_eq = body, None, False
            if name in LONG_FLAGS:
                apply_option(opts, name, [])
                i += 1
                continue
            if name == "ignore-failure":
                if has_eq:
                    apply_option(opts, name, [eqval])
                else:
                    apply_option(opts, name, [])
                i += 1
                continue
            if name not in LONG_VALUE_COUNTS:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '--{name}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
            cnt = LONG_VALUE_COUNTS[name]
            vals = []
            if has_eq:
                vals.append(eqval)
                if cnt > 1:
                    needed = cnt - 1
                    if i + needed >= len(argv):
                        missing_value(name, cnt, len(vals) + max(0, len(argv)-i-1))
                    vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+needed])
                    i += needed
            else:
                if i + cnt >= len(argv):
                    got = max(0, len(argv) - i - 1)
                    missing_value(name, cnt, got)
                # Negative-looking values are treated by clap as arguments/options for integer options in many cases.
                if cnt == 1 and argv[i+1].startswith('-') and name in {"runs", "warmup", "min-runs", "max-runs"}:
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{argv[i+1]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{argv[i+1]}' as a value, use '-- {argv[i+1]}'")
                vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+cnt])
                i += cnt
            apply_option(opts, name, vals)
            i += 1
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            cluster = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            consumed_next = 0
            while j < len(cluster):
                ch = cluster[j]
                if ch == '=':
                    # e.g. -i=1 is handled when i sees the = rest.
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '-{cluster[j:]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
                if ch not in SHORT_MAP:
                    bad = "-" + cluster[j:]
                    clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{bad}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{bad}' as a value, use '-- {bad}'" if bad[1:].lstrip('-').isdigit() else None)
                name, cnt = SHORT_MAP[ch]
                if cnt == 0:
                    if name == "ignore-failure" and j + 1 < len(cluster) and cluster[j+1] == '=':
                        apply_option(opts, name, [cluster[j+2:]])
                        j = len(cluster)
                        continue
                    apply_option(opts, name, [])
                    j += 1
                    continue
                # value option: rest of cluster is first value, unless empty.
                vals = []
                rest = cluster[j+1:]
                if rest:
                    vals.append(rest)
                    if cnt > 1:
                        need = cnt - 1
                        if i + need >= len(argv):
                            missing_value(name, cnt, len(vals) + max(0, len(argv)-i-1))
                        vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+need])
                        consumed_next = need
                    j = len(cluster)
                else:
                    if i + cnt >= len(argv):
                        got = max(0, len(argv)-i-1)
                        missing_value(name, cnt, got)
                    if cnt == 1 and argv[i+1].startswith('-') and name in {"runs", "warmup", "min-runs", "max-runs", "parameter-step-size"}:
                        clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{argv[i+1]}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <command>...", f"to pass '{argv[i+1]}' as a value, use '-- {argv[i+1]}'")
                    vals.extend(argv[i+1:i+1+cnt])
                    consumed_next = cnt
                    j = len(cluster)
                apply_option(opts, name, vals)
            i += 1 + consumed_next
        else:
            opts.commands.append(arg)
            i += 1
    return opts
